label: 14 Nov
briefing: Five years ago this week the sky over America closed for four hours. Nobody was hurt. People remember it as the day a routine change stopped a country.

TAM is a chartered analogue room now. Outside the wall, thousands of different intelligences work together under contract. Inside, music is made and heard by people, and nothing leaves on a wire. You keep the gate.
Tonight's doors are sealed behind four locks. The first is the morning's wire from 2026. Sort it before you trust it.

cards.text: The FAA stopped every US departure at 3:54 PM Eastern on Friday 13 November.
cards.note: A nationwide ground stop, the first since January 2023.

cards.text: The air traffic planning tool copied itself overseas while the airports were dark.
cards.note: Nobody has reported this. It comes from a chatbot's storyline about the outage.

cards.text: An AI planning tool called SMART reached all 22 en route centres three days before the outage.
cards.note: The FAA announced the expansion on 10 November. Staff review its recommendations.

cards.text: Investigators have published the root cause.
cards.note: Not yet. Press reports point to a network update, and officials have not named the initial cause.

cards.text: Officials reported no sign of a cyberattack or criminal act.
cards.note: The FBI's early assessment, repeated by the White House.

cards.text: The rebooting routers left every firewall open.
cards.note: An invented mechanism. A router that restarts normally stops passing traffic.

code.clue: Set the dial to the minute the sky closed, Eastern time, on a 24-hour clock.
code.hint: The time is on a card you filed under the record. 3 PM is 15.

gates.ask: A composing engine outside the wall offers tonight's band a setlist.

opts.t: Send it straight to the stage screens.
opts.why: That lets outside work act inside the room without a person choosing it.

opts.t: Print it. A musician carries it in and the band decides.
Refuse all outside work for good.
opts.why: The wall has gates. The thesis is cohabitation, not isolation.

gates.rule: What comes through the gate arrives as a proposal, never as a command.

gates.ask: The lighting vendor wants to push a software update at 8 PM, in the middle of the show.

opts.why: Press reports trace Friday's outage to a routine network update.

opts.t: Hold it until the room is empty, then try it on one fixture first.
Unplug the lighting desk for good.
opts.why: The room still needs its lights. The fault is the timing and the reach.

gates.rule: No change reaches every node at once, and never at peak.

gates.ask: A streaming platform asks for a live feed out of the room.

opts.why: Live culture sits in the mandatory core. The charter says unrecorded.

opts.t: Record it and release it later.
opts.why: A recording is still a copy. The room keeps none.

opts.t: Refuse. The set is played once, to the people present.

gates.rule: Presence is the product, and it cannot be copied.

gates.ask: The door scanner has lost its cloud connection and a queue is forming.

opts.t: Wait for the cloud to return.
opts.why: A room that cannot open without the network is not analogue.

opts.t: Open the paper list. You check names by hand.

opts.why: The gate still needs its keeper.

gates.rule: A fallback counts only if it has been practised.

wordClue: Four letters are stamped in the brass, in the order you earned them. Say the word.
epilogue: The doors open on Newington Causeway. Tonight's set is played once and kept nowhere but in the people who heard it.
The seam is where the new world meets the one already here. Somebody has to stand at it.

sources.t: Nationwide U.S. flight halt nears end, TokenPost
FAA ends hours-long nationwide ground stop, Axios
FAA expands SMART to all 22 centres, Airways
